summary: Checks whether a value is a Ui object.
description: An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "Ui"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is a Ui object; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
const ui = SpreadsheetApp.getUi();

isUi(ui); // => true
isUi({}); // => false
isUi(null); // => false
```
